name: Big Thief
label: 4AD
lede: Two Berklee alumni and two friends spent years living on the road, then made an 80-minute double album in five studios during lockdown, and Pitchfork ranked it No. 7 of 2022.

eras.title: Two songwriters, no band yet
eras.text: Adrianne Lenker was making solo records from her teens; Buck Meek was a Texas-born guitarist busking in New York subway stations. Both had passed through Berklee, and by 2013 they were touring as a duo.

years.h: Adrianne Lenker's first solo record, Stages of the Sun
years.p: Wikipedia dates [[Adrianne Lenker|763cb144-afdb-471e-bd86-d4f5b9b58641]]'s solo career to 2006, when the Minnesota-raised songwriter was around 15.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Stages of the Sun (2006) as the start of her discography, which means she was writing and releasing music a decade before Big Thief's debut. She was homeschooled, got her GED at 16 and later went to Berklee College of Music on a scholarship from Susan Tedeschi, according to her Wikipedia biography.

years.src: Wikipedia: Big Thief · The Line of Best Fit
years.h: Lenker and Buck Meek tour as a duo
years.p: Before there were four of them, it was two guitars and two voices, working out the songs that would become Big Thief's.
years.xp: Wikipedia says [[Adrianne Lenker|763cb144-afdb-471e-bd86-d4f5b9b58641]] and [[Buck Meek|b8780175-4ff4-4d87-8e54-999f70dbb5ec]] met at a show in Boston and reconnected in Brooklyn. Lenker told The Line of Best Fit she met Meek on her first day in New York, at 21. Either way, the duo toured in 2013, and in 2014 released two EPs, a-sides and b-sides.

years.h: Hours Were the Birds: Lenker's second solo album
years.p: She self-released it in 2014; Saddle Creek reissued it in 2018, after Big Thief had made her name.

eras.title: A lake house, a van, a first record
eras.text: Big Thief became a band in 2015 and then mostly stopped having an address. They made two albums for Saddle Creek in fourteen months and toured both of them until NPR and Spin noticed.

years.src: The Line of Best Fit · Wikipedia: Big Thief
years.h: Max Oleartchik and James Krivchenia complete the band
years.p: Bassist Oleartchik was a Berklee friend of Buck Meek's; Krivchenia started as the engineer on the record and ended up on drums.
years.xp: According to The Line of Best Fit, Lenker and Meek bumped into Oleartchik on a New York street after about ten years. Jason Burger briefly played drums in 2015 (Wikipedia spells it Burger; the Line of Best Fit prints Berger) before Krivchenia, who had been engineering their record, took the kit.

years.cap: Big Thief at Haldern Pop Festival 2018 in Haldern · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Masterpiece (Big Thief album) · The Line of Best Fit
years.h: Twelve days in a great-aunt's house on Lake Champlain
years.p: The band cut Masterpiece in a friend's great-aunt's lake house in Essex, New York, with [[Andrew Sarlo|700b0a0c-9c3b-44b3-8de4-51c1a5f4b2e1]] producing.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the sessions to July 1–12, 2015. The Line of Best Fit reports the album came out "untouched and unchanged," exactly as they recorded it. Sarlo, Lenker's friend from Berklee, went on to work on the band's records for years.

years.h: Masterpiece: a debut that bets on the title
years.p: Saddle Creek put it out as a 12-track record; Pitchfork gave it 7.7 and Metacritic averaged 79 from 14 reviews.
years.xp: The cover is a photograph of Lenker's mother as a child, playing with a toy dinosaur. Wikipedia lists lovesickness, abuse and mental illness among its subjects, in songs that shift between lo-fi acoustic and loud, hooky rock.

years.src: NPR Music: Big Thief Tiny Desk Concert · Wikipedia: Big Thief
years.h: Big Thief play the NPR Tiny Desk
years.p: Their first NPR Tiny Desk concert, a few months after the debut album came out.
years.xp: NPR's page for the session is dated August 2016. NPR's Bob Boilen had already written that Big Thief were "a band bound by great songs," per Wikipedia.

years.h: Capacity: the record that puts them on year-end lists
years.p: Recorded over a month in a house-sat farmhouse, it scored 8.3 at Pitchfork and ended up No. 2 on Spin's 50 best albums of 2017.
years.xp: "Mythological Beauty" premiered on NPR on April 4, 2017, and closing track "Mary" later landed at No. 44 on Pitchfork's 200 best songs of the 2010s. The cover is a photo of Lenker's uncle holding her as an infant. Sources differ on NPR's placement: Wikipedia's Big Thief page credits Boilen's personal top ten with it at No. 1, the Capacity page says No. 3.

eras.title: Woods and desert: two albums, one year
eras.text: Big Thief signed to 4AD and made two records back to back: U.F.O.F. in the Washington woods, Two Hands in the Texas desert. The first one made them a Grammy-nominated band.

years.h: Lenker's Abysskiss and Meek's debut arrive; their marriage ends
years.p: Lenker put out Abysskiss on Saddle Creek and Meek his first solo album on Keeled Scales; Wikipedia says they divorced in 2018.
years.xp: Wikipedia's Meek page gives their marriage as 2012–2018. They remained bandmates and collaborators. Two songs from Abysskiss, "From" and "Terminal Paradise," came back in different form on U.F.O.F.

years.cap: Big Thief performing at The National's Homecoming festival in Cincinnati, Ohio - April… · Wikimedia
years.src: The FADER: Big Thief escaped · Wikipedia: U.F.O.F.
years.h: Bear Creek: a hot tub, a treehouse and a first-take "Cattails"
years.p: The band recorded U.F.O.F. live in one big room at Bear Creek Studio, Woodinville, Washington, with [[Andrew Sarlo|700b0a0c-9c3b-44b3-8de4-51c1a5f4b2e1]] producing.
years.xp: Engineer [[Dom Monks|d5ccfcad-1071-4ec0-acea-0e5260e39b6d]] "sneaks mics up" rather than stopping the room, The FADER reported, so "Cattails" was already captured by the time the band finished playing it. Lenker wrote "Century" on the grass at the studio. Drummer James Krivchenia ran every track through a "Magic Box" of knobs, a kind of treatment unavailable on earlier records.

years.h: U.F.O.F.: first record for 4AD, first 9.2 from Pitchfork
years.p: Pitchfork called it Best New Music; Metacritic averages 87, and three sold-out release shows ran May 2–5 in Los Angeles and Brooklyn.
years.xp: The title stands for "UFO friend." Pitchfork's Jeremy Larson called it "a mesmerizing flood of life filtered down into a concentrated drip" per Wikipedia. It later made Pitchfork's 200 best albums of the 2010s at No. 33.

years.big: "We didn't want to make a double album."
q: We didn't want to make a double album.
years.src: Stereogum: Big Thief's Big Year · Wikipedia: Big Thief
years.h: Two Hands: the desert twin, cut at Sonic Ranch
years.p: Recorded at Sonic Ranch in Tornillo, Texas, about 30 miles from El Paso, and released five months after U.F.O.F.
years.xp: Lenker told Stereogum the two records were meant to contrast: U.F.O.F. ethereal and layered, Two Hands raw, live and plain. "We didn't want to make a double album, because we felt it was too dense," she said. Three years later they made one anyway.

years.h: U.F.O.F. gets a Grammy nomination for Best Alternative Music Album
years.p: Big Thief's first Grammy nod; "Not" from Two Hands followed at the 2021 ceremony for Best Rock Song and Best Rock Performance.

eras.title: Lockdown, and forty-five songs
eras.text: With touring shut, the band did something they had not had time for in five years: stay put. Lenker released her own records, and the band spent months building what became their biggest album.

years.h: Songs and Instrumentals: Lenker goes solo on 4AD
years.p: Lenker put out the paired records Songs and Instrumentals on 4AD in 2020, the year after Big Thief's two albums.

years.cap: Big Thief at the Lexington · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You · Wikipedia: Big Thief
years.h: Five studios, five months, 45 songs
years.p: From April to December 2020 the band recorded in Massachusetts, upstate New York, California, Colorado and Arizona, then cut 45 songs to 20.
years.xp: Wikipedia's album page lists the Elf Inn (Westhampton, Massachusetts), Flying Cloud Recordings (upstate New York), Five Star Studios (Topanga), MusicGardens (Colorado) and Press On Studio (Tucson). Krivchenia produced; it was the first Big Thief record without Sarlo in the chair. Wikipedia's Big Thief page adds a two-week quarantine in the Vermont woods in July 2020.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You
years.h: "Little Things" and "Sparrow" announce the new record
years.p: "Little Things" got Best New Track from Pitchfork and ranked No. 15 on its best songs of 2021.

years.h: "Certainty" goes out as the second single
years.p: The song would go on to a Grammy nomination for Best Alternative Music Performance.

years.h: "Change" is the third single
years.p: Pitchfork later called the album a "20-song epic," and this was its third advance track.

eras.title: The double album everyone ranked
eras.text: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You came out in February 2022 and did what Big Thief's fans had hoped: it landed near the top of a dozen year-end lists. The year also tested the band in public.

years.cap: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You (4AD, 2022)
years.src: Wikipedia: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You
years.h: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You: 20 songs, 80 minutes
years.p: Pitchfork gave the 4AD double album 9.0 and ranked it No. 7 of 2022; Metacritic averages 88.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Andy Cush called it "a 20-song epic of kaleidoscopic invention, striking beauty, and wigged-out humor," per Wikipedia. [[Mat Davidson|e4547aac-28f7-40f3-9a98-080034f3069d]] (Twain) plays fiddle and sings throughout, the first big fifth voice on a Big Thief record, and [[James Krivchenia|611cb5a3-42cd-4aef-98e6-5749b88bf63a]] produced. Christgau gave it an A; AllMusic's 3.5 stars said it "lands much more like a showreel than a plotted album."

The 2022 singles ran from "Little Things" and "Certainty" through "Time Escaping," "No Reason" and "Simulation Swarm."

years.src: Stereogum: Big Thief Cancel Tel Aviv Shows · Wikipedia: Big Thief
years.h: Big Thief book Tel Aviv, then cancel both shows
years.p: The band first said it wanted to play Oleartchik's hometown, then apologized for "the recklessness and naivete of our original statement" and pulled the July 6–7 dates.
years.xp: Stereogum reported that the first statement acknowledged the BDS movement, said the band did not claim to know where "the moral high ground lies," and pledged profits to Palestinian humanitarian groups. The reversal said they opposed the occupation and believed in "total freedom and self-determination for all Palestinians." The venue, Barby, posted an angry Hebrew response, and Consequence reported it called the band "cowards."

years.src: Consequence: Big Thief Happiness Tiny Desk
years.h: Tiny Desk (Home) concert with an unreleased song
years.p: Big Thief played "Happiness," a track that hadn't been released, in their second NPR Tiny Desk appearance.

years.h: Year-end lists: Paste No. 1, The Atlantic No. 2, Pitchfork No. 7
years.p: Wikipedia also lists NPR Music at No. 4, Uncut at No. 5 and Rolling Stone at No. 35 of 100.

years.h: Two Grammy nominations for Dragon
years.p: Best Alternative Music Album for the record, plus Best Alternative Music Performance for "Certainty."

years.h: Buck Meek's Haunted Mountain lands on 4AD
years.p: Meek's third solo album, after Buck Meek (2018) and Two Saviors (2021), was his first for the label.

eras.title: Three and a fraction
eras.text: Max Oleartchik left after nine years, the band decided not to replace him, and Big Thief kept making records in bigger rooms with more guests. The band is active.

years.h: Bright Future: Lenker's 4AD record gets a Grammy nod
years.p: Her 2024 solo album was nominated for Best Folk Album; Wikipedia counts five Grammy nominations for her overall.

years.src: Wikipedia: Big Thief · Wikipedia: Double Infinity
years.h: Max Oleartchik leaves, citing "interpersonal reasons"
years.p: The band said they'd end nine years with "mutual respect in our hearts"; on July 28 they played Project Pabst in Portland with a five-piece lineup.
years.xp: Wikipedia's Big Thief page dates his departure to June 2024; the Double Infinity page says July. The Portland show was the band's first in almost a year, with bassist Justin Felton and second percussionist Jon Nellen, and ten live debuts in a 14-song set.

years.h: Double Infinity: three members, ten session players
years.p: Recorded in three weeks at Power Station in New York with producer [[Dom Monks|d5ccfcad-1071-4ec0-acea-0e5260e39b6d]], it drew a 7.6 from Pitchfork.
years.xp: Rather than hire a bassist, Lenker, Meek and Krivchenia invited session players including [[Laraaji|249e0ab9-2690-47f3-8c9a-ef7bb62ee466]]. Lenker said the band "can expand and contract." Metacritic averages 84, and Mojo ranked it No. 4 of 2025.

years.cap: Ryman Auditorium, Nashville. Image to source.
years.h: At the Ryman: all 29 songs of Horsepower, played in full
years.p: Two nights, a table onstage, and guests including [[Lucinda Williams|21685b15-3074-446e-aa1d-ff7157014f53]], Gillian Welch, Iris DeMent and Rodney Crowell.
years.xp: Per JamBase, the triple album was recorded in Nashville in May 2026 and played in non-sequential order; both nights were professionally filmed. Lenker and Meek said the album is targeted for spring 2027.
